key_highlights: ASX finished flat with miners outperforming while oil stocks struggled; IDP saw a sharp decline (#40)
Australian flash PMI sags, signalling softening domestic demand amid RBA rate-hike cycle squeezing household spending (#55, #61)
Saudi oil shock drives Australian fuel prices higher, pressuring transport and consumer sectors (#69, #34)

Gold and rare-earths miners active: Critical Resources surges on Suriname gold, Aurum raises $52.5M, Platina receives final Rio cheque, Critica secures Jupiter rare-earths offtake (#45, #46, #68, #44)
Tech stocks lead ASX higher post Wall Street surge; $16B Aussie tech firm faces China-link controversy (#66, #37)
10-year US Treasury yield at highest since 2007, pricing in further Fed hikes; global risk-off mood (#7, #25)
Jetstar staff escalate industrial action, waiving baggage/seat fees; Qantas confirms Sydney-New York non-stop launch (#63, #50)

sectors.trend: Miners rose on the ASX, led by gold and rare-earths names. Critical Resources surged on Suriname gold; Aurum raised $52.5M for West African gold; Platina banked final Rio cheque; Critica secured Jupiter rare-earths offtake. Iron ore/coal muted amid China rebalancing towards robots.
sectors.implications: Gold miners (GOLD.AX, NGX.AX) and rare-earths (CRL.AX, CRG.AX) offer relative strength. BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face headwinds from China property uncertainty and robot-driven industrial shift. Diversified miners preferred over single-commodity exposure.

sectors.trend: Oil stocks struggled on the ASX despite a Saudi oil shock spiking global crude. Australian fuel prices surging as global buffers dry up. Nuclear energy debate and energy-cost politics add policy uncertainty. Commonwealth to fund abandoned WA oil platform decommissioning.
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WLE.AX, XAR.AX face margin pressure from input costs. Woodside and Santos benefit from higher gas prices but face political headwinds. Nuclear debate could reshape long-term energy mix. Fuel-cost inflation pressures WES.AX, WTW.AX.

sectors.trend: RBA rate-hike cycle squeezing household spending and credit demand. Flash PMI weakness signals slowing economic momentum. Government debt trajectory raises fiscal risk. BDC debt pressure in software sector globally.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX benefit from higher NIMs but face rising credit losses as households struggle. Property lenders exposed to falling prices. Monitor RBA next meeting closely.

sectors.trend: Tech led ASX higher after Wall Street surge. $16B Aussie tech firm in China-link controversy. Data centres straining net-zero targets. Global chip stocks pulled back after six-day rally; Burry shorting Micron/Palantir.
sectors.implications: ASX tech names (W1.AX, XRO.AX, SVL.AX) benefit from global AI momentum but face China-geopolitical risk. Chip pullback (SOX) may cool sentiment. Data-centre power demand supports energy infrastructure plays.

sectors.trend: Syngenis gains precision-medicine firepower. Jetstar industrial action escalates. Qantas confirms SYD-JFK non-stop. Property listings rising, demand falling. El Niño threatens agricultural output.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX, SYG.AX (if listed) benefit from healthcare innovation. QAN.AX, JQZ.AX face operational disruption from Jetstar action. REITs (GPW.AX, ICPL.AX) pressured by falling property prices. El Niño risk to WBC.AX agribusiness.

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely range-bound to mildly negative. RBA tightening, PMI weakness, and fuel-price inflation cap upside. Gold/rare-earths and tech provide pockets of strength. Jetstar action and property cooling add volatility. 10-year yield spike may trigger risk-off flows into AUD.
market_outlook.long_term: 6–12 month outlook cautiously constructive if RBA pivots and PMI stabilises. Gold and rare-earths structural demand supports materials. Energy transition (nuclear debate, data-centre power) creates multi-year themes. Property correction may create entry points for quality REITs by late 2026. China rebalancing towards robots could lift industrial/tech demand.
